MATTHEVV.|29}}</noinclude>lesser in the kingdom of heauen, is greater then he. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 16, 16.''}}* from the dayes of Iohn the Baptist vntil novv, the kingdom of heauen suffereth violence, and the violent beare it avvay. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† For al the Prophets and the Lavv prophecied vnto Iohn: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† and if you vvil receiue it, he is {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 4, 5.''}}* ‖ Elias that is for to come. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 7, 31.''}}* vvherevnto shal I esteeme this generation to be like? It is like to children sitting in the market-place: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† vvhich crying to their companions, say, We haue piped to you, and you haue not daunced: we haue lamented, and you haue not mourned. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† For {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 4.''}}* Iohn came neither eating nor drinking: and they say, He hath a diuel. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† The Sonne of man came ‖ eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man that is a glotton and a vvinedrinker, a frende of Publicans and sinners. And vvisedom is iustified of her children.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† Then {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 10, 13.''}}* began he to vpbraide the cities, vvherein vvere done the most of his miracles, for that they had not done penance. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}}† Wo be to thee Corozain, vvo be to thee Beth-saida: for if in Tyre & Sidon had been vvrought the miracles that haue been vvrought in you, they had done ‖ penance in hearecloth and ashes long agoe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}}† But neuerthelesse, I say to you, it shal be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of iudgement, then for you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}}† And thou Capharnaum, shalt thou be exalted vp to heauen? thou shalt come dovvne euen vnto hel. for if in Sodom had been vvrought the miracles that haue been wrought in thee, perhaps it had remained vnto this day. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}}† But notvvithstanding I say to you, that it shal be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of iudgement, then for thee.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=25}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Matthias day Feb. 24. and vpon S. Francis day Octob. 4. and for many Martyrs.}}At that time IESVS ansvvered and said. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 10, 21.''}}* I confesse to thee O Father lord of heauen and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the vvise and prudent, and hast reuealed thē to ‖ litle ones. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=26}}† Yea Father: for so hath it vvel pleased thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=27}}† Al things are deliuered me of my Father. And no man knovveth the Sonne but the Father: neither doth any knovv the Father, but the Sonne, and to vvhom it shal please the Sonne to reueale. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=28}}† Come ye to me al that labour, and are burdened, and I vvil refresh you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=29}}† Take vp my yoke vpon you, and learne of me, because I am meeke, and humble of hart: and you shal finde rest to your soules. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=30}}† For my ‖ yoke is svveete, and my burden light.⊣<noinclude>{{rh||D iij|Annot-}}</noinclude>
